llm.summary: The skill's files and instructions are consistent with an nginx configuration and basic server-operations helper; nothing appears to request unrelated credentials or download external code, but it does read local system state and writes to a user data directory so review before use.

dimensions.detail: The name/description (nginx config, reverse proxy, SSL, caching, security, optimization) matches the provided generator (scripts/nginx.sh) and helper (scripts/script.sh). The included scripts produce nginx config snippets and provide simple sysadmin helpers, which is coherent with a server/ops oriented tool.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md directs the agent to use the included CLI (nginx-config). The scripts themselves read local system state (e.g., /proc/cpuinfo, /var/log/syslog) and print commands like systemctl restart and tar; SKILL.md does not explicitly instruct broad data collection or network transmission, but the scripts can expose local system information when run. This is expected for a system-ops helper but worth noting.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only), which is the lowest installation risk. The package does include shell scripts (no external downloads), so there is code to execute but nothing is fetched from external/untrusted URLs.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or credentials. The scripts do honor/consult common env vars (NGINX_CONFIG_DIR, XDG_DATA_HOME, HOME) and create files under the user's data directory (~/.local/share/nginx-config). No secrets or unrelated cloud credentials are requested, but the use of environment variables and file writes is not documented in SKILL.md.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false (no forced inclusion). The scripts create and write logs/history to a per-user data directory; they do not modify other skills or system configuration automatically. They output commands (e.g., systemctl restart) but do not execute privileged system changes themselves.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to be what it says: a generator for nginx configs plus small sysadmin helpers. Before installing or running it: (1) review the scripts locally — they are plain shell and readable; (2) be aware the helper script reads /proc and /var/log/syslog and writes logs to a per-user data directory (~/.local/share/nginx-config by default); (3) the scripts print commands that could be run manually (systemctl restart, tar) but do not execute privileged operations by themselves — do not run printed commands unless you trust them; (4) ensure your agent or tooling won't forward sensitive outputs (logs, system info) to external services; and (5) if you want stricter isolation, run the scripts in a test VM or container before using on production systems.
